description: Korean Hroparts TYPE-C-31-M-12 — 16-pin USB-C receptacle, surface-mount with through-hole shield-retention tabs. 5 A / 20 V rated, 10 000 mating cycles. The most common low-cost USB-C connector for maker boards; KiCad ships a matching footprint as USB_C_Receptacle_HRO_TYPE-C-31-M-12.
name: usb-c-16p
watch_out_for: CRITICAL: install 5.1 kΩ resistors to GND on BOTH CC1 and CC2 (one EACH, separately — NEVER tie them together). Without these, USB-C source chargers will refuse to enumerate as a UFP and the board will see 0 V on VBUS. Shield tabs are through-hole for mechanical strength — design the PCB with the matching THT holes through-shield-clearance pad sizes or the connector will tear off after a few insertions. USB 2.0 data pins only (D+/D−); not wired for USB 3.0 SuperSpeed pairs. SBU1/SBU2 are unused for plain 2.0 — leave unconnected. Verify both rows of D+/D− are bridged on the PCB so the cable orientation doesn't matter.
